description:
Looks up an IP address, domain, URL or file hash, such as one from a message, log line, SIEM alert or code under review.

Look up a single indicator of compromise (IP, domain, URL, or hash) in the DugganUSA corpus. Returns the threat type, malware family, confidence and references of the record with the strongest attribution (first-party, then curated, then third-party; not necessarily the highest confidence), the attributed actor if any record names one, and a `sources` list with each record's source, actor, confidence, first-seen date (when it entered our corpus, not when it was first observed) and description (up to 10). `attribution` names the strongest record's class. Read-only. Country is filled in only when the source records one; many feeds publish none.

Useful after `search` finds something, for the full attribution and cross-feed correlation, or directly when triaging a single indicator.

Pass the IOC as either `indicator` or `value` (both work). Optional `type` hint: ip / domain / url / hash / auto.

Examples:
  indicator="185.93.3.195" → ShinyHunters/UNC6040 infrastructure.
  indicator="goldenleafway.lat" → fresh Apothecary/ClearFake .lat rotation domain.
  indicator="ee28b3137d65d74c0234eea35fa536af" → Volexity-attributed malware MD5 (BrazenBamboo/DEEPDATA campaign).

Returns `found: false` when the indicator isn't in the corpus. That means we hold no record, not that it is safe.

indicator.description: The indicator to enrich (IP, domain, URL, or hash).
